titleStmt.title: No. 903
The Secretary of State to the Embassy in Egypt

div.head:
No. 903
The Secretary of State to the Embassy in Egypt
div.p:
541. Eban his request called Murphy Oct. 1. Recounted events surrounding detention Bat Galim at Suez by Egyptians. Formally
assured USG vessel was unarmed and engaged in no aggressive acts. Dismissed Egypt’s allegations of hostile acts as complete fabrication. Stated Egyptian story had been received with “injured skepticism” by majority delegations at UN well as UNSYG and President SC.

Eban recapitulated legal basis 1951 SC resolution calling upon Egypt open Canal to Israel shipping. Stated problem had recently assumed increased importance Israel for two reasons: 1) Economic. Blockade of Canal hurting trade between Israel and countries of Africa and Asia such as Ethiopia, Thailand and Burma with whom Israel had hopes increasing trade. Prevention supply Iranian oil to Israel was costing country $10 to 15 million annually. Israel had been able carry on some trade through Canal by use other flag vessels but this in many cases involved embroilment third country in Israel-Egyptian dispute and it was becoming increasingly difficult find willing third party carriers. 2) Political. IG did not feel UK had been sufficiently vigilant in its efforts preserve freedom of navigation Canal. Israel therefore felt that before Egypt was left by world as undisputed sole possessor Suez Canal area her good intentions should be tested. Eban admitted Bat Galim had been test case and stated test cases were legitimate practice in international law.
Israel had hoped Egypt would have permitted vessel to pass. Israel had given notice to SC in May she would attempt achieve progressive relaxation Egyptian restrictions.

Israel would be taking matter up formally with SC if that body were not “veto-ridden.” Israel had not ruled out possibility USSR might even support her at this time. Eban noted that USSR had taken up matter freedom navigation China Sea with SC on Sept. 30. On balance however Israel preferred avoid SC if possible. UNSYG had stated to Eban that because of weakness of SC, good officers were better in this situation. UNSYG plans speak to Egyptian representative in UN on this matter. Israel also requests US seek release vessel from Egyptian authorities. IG is encouraged by fact Egyptian Government has so far not committed itself to non-release of vessel. GOE justified detention on basis alleged shooting incidents. Should these allegations be proved unfounded way would be clear for vessel’s release. If UNSYG and US efforts failed IG would have no alternative but approach to SC.
Murphy informed Eban Department would look into matter and informed IG.
Department realizes all facts this case not yet in. Impression this stage however particularly in view Embtel 436 is Egypt may have

“I asked him ‘are reports that Israelis fired on Egyptian fishermen and killed them correct?’ He said (in strict confidence) ‘until investigations now underway are complete I will not say definitely.’” (984A.53/10–154)
fallen into Israel’s well set trap through seizure by Egyptian authorities acting without prior top level clearance. Having learned of seizure Salem may have swiftly fabricated story of firing and succeeded reaching US headlines first with this version. NY Times tone skeptical in reporting it. Department wonders whether GOE in pulling forth its version has not seized upon only possible excuse for seizure vessel under self-defense clauses 1888 Convention which would prima facie accord with generally accepted interpretations that convention. Thus GOE not interfering with Canal traffic per se but taking military action against vessel which had first attacked.

If foregoing interpretation approximates truth Department would hope this implies 1) seizure of vessel not supported by Nasir and 2) GOE had not intended continue restrictions on Canal traffic but on contrary quietly drop them.

Department working level has already expressed concern Egyptian Embassy over unfortunate timing this occurrence and has requested details. You are requested informally convey Foreign Minister following reflections: 1) USG realizes all details re this incident not yet fully clarified, 2) meanwhile seizure vessel comes at most inopportune time, 3) USG interested in avoiding further publicity and SC consideration this incident and conceivable situation where USG obliged again take public stand basis SC resolution 1951, 4) USG therefore hopes GOE will find it possible soon release vessel for Suez transit if allegations of shooting prove unfounded.

Unless you see serious objections you should add that US continues believe Egypt’s own interests would be best served by allowing unrestricted traffic through Suez. (Any Egyptian action in this regard need not be specifically related to Israel traffic through Canal.) We take this position not only because of our disapproval Egypt’s failure comply with SC resolution September 1, 1951 but also because we anticipate there will be continuing unpleasant cases if Egypt detains Israeli ships or cargoes in future. Israel will unquestionably continue make capital of such detentions and USG will be obliged support her right of free transit pursuant to SC resolution and our interpretation self-defense clause 1888 Convention. Result will be harmful a) to US-Egyptian relations, b) to our common efforts reduce Near East tensions and c) to prospects for increased mutually beneficial collaboration between Egypt and
West which Nasir has clearly stated he desires and which is our avowed policy. USG hopes and believes it can work quietly and intimately with GOE to avoid all situations which embarrass our common effort to play down Arab-Israel issue and our mutual desire strengthen NE against Soviet danger.
Since drafting foregoing Israel Embassy has today notified Department Israel has submitted matter SC on instructions from Jerusalem. No explanation offered for this apparent shift in tactics.

note.p: Repeated to Tel Aviv, London, Paris, and Damascus; sent by pouch to Amman, Baghdad, Beirut, Jidda, Port Said, and New York.
The memorandum of this conversation is in file 674.84A/10–154.
In telegram 436 from Cairo, Oct. 1, 2 p.m., Caffery reported:

“Egyptian Minister Foreign Affairs confirmed to me this morning that he had sent instructions to Egyptian representatives at New York to bring case of Israeli ship Bat Galim to attention of Presidents of UNGA and SC, for information only.

On Oct. 4, Israel requested that a meeting of the Security Council be called to consider the earlier Israeli complaint against Egypt concerning Egyptian restrictions on the passage through the Suez Canal of ships trading with Israel. (U.N. doc. S/3300)
The Bat Galim was discussed by the Security Councill between its 682d and 686th meetings, from Oct. 14 to Dec. 7. (U.N. docs. S/PV.682–686)
